title: How to set up events and revenue tracking in DataFast
description: Practical DataFast setup for web analytics goals and payment-linked revenue attribution — including cookieless mode trade-offs for indie SaaS.
quickAnswer: **DataFast** covers lightweight web analytics plus optional **payment attribution** (e.g. Stripe). Set up the site script first, define goals/funnels you need, then connect payments and pass visitor/session ids into checkout metadata so revenue ties back to channels.

sections.title: Install the script first
sections.content:
Add DataFast via snippet, npm, or the CMS path that matches your stack. Confirm pageviews and referrers before you chase revenue joins.

Choose **default vs cookieless** deliberately — cookieless can ease consent friction but changes identity. We recorded both installs: [default](/benchmarks/datafast-script-2026-09/) and [cookieless](/benchmarks/datafast-cookieless-script-2026-09/).

sections.title: Goals and funnels
sections.content: Define goals for the marketing actions that matter (pricing click, signup). Keep the list short. DataFast is closer to web analytics than full product analytics — see [DataFast vs PostHog](/compare/datafast-vs-posthog/) if you need deep in-app events.

sections.title: Connect revenue attribution
sections.content:
For Stripe-style flows: connect the provider, then pass DataFast visitor/session identifiers into checkout or payment metadata so paid conversions inherit channel and referrer context.

QA with a test payment and confirm the sale appears with traffic source attached. Missing metadata is the usual failure mode.

sections.title: When DataFast is the wrong event tool
sections.content:
If your primary need is feature flags, session replay, or complex product funnels, instrument PostHog (or similar) in the app and keep DataFast for marketing + revenue questions — or pick one stack consciously.

Compare cost and fit with [Plausible vs DataFast](/compare/plausible-vs-datafast/) and the [pricing calculator](/calculators/pricing/).
